findings.explanation: The root-to-subdataset links and concrete file accesses expose the paper computation boundary. The unresolved acquisition-source repository is not read by the paper procedures, so excluding regeneration of acquisition files is an explicit, defensible scope decision.

The inspected loader reaches benchmark annotations through the implementation submodule; other functions consume exported gaze files and event TSVs in the named data modules. Both categories are explicitly connected. Missing cohort payloads do not establish missing references.

The recipe covers the analysis/rendering tools, configuration declares the adapter invocation, and script/Make definitions expose settings and defaults. This supports presence of dependencies and settings without implying frozen dependency resolution.

Separate license texts are reachable along the actual module links. The inspected labels inventory and README supply no governing declaration; therefore complete coverage cannot be awarded. Container-internal license coverage remains uninspected rather than demonstrated absent.

Read-only ls-tree confirms the three exact gitlinks. The frozen inventory records file object IDs and annex content keys; image metadata identifies exact configuration and layers. Identification is supported independently of possession of their bytes.

Git objects, nested gitlinks and git-annex keys provide a compatible root tracking view across the declared research payload classes. Externally installed orchestration prerequisites should remain explicitly distinguished from payloads, as this assessment does.

Root and linked histories record actors, times and descriptions, including manual figure changes and data generation. The histogram addition is itself recorded even though its execution lacks an automatic run record. That distinction supports the high modification-history rating.

The numerical run and label-generation record contain captured commands and input/output fields. The histogram commit instead retrospectively names quality_stats, and that function is absent from the captured main CLI. Partial automatic provenance is demonstrated; all-step coverage is not.

The root execution has Git-linked code/data/configuration and an explicit image input. The label record invokes host Python without identifying its environment state, while the image build depends on moving package resolution. These are concrete limits to an all-executions/all-components claim.

The cached tag object contains a PGP signature and names its target. Neither its message nor the inspected README supplies an identity/key-verification route. Zero is defensible under the complete binary anchor; this is not a finding that the signature is invalid.
findings.suggested_correction: For precise citation, cite the immutable tag object as well as its target: a commit-tree URL alone does not expose the signed tag object.

findings.explanation: The documented clone/rerun sequence plus captured input patterns covers component acquisition. Raw data documentation additionally describes annex initialization and retrieval. This supports instructional completeness, distinct from whether all remote payloads are currently obtainable.

A concrete container-based setup route and tool-installation references are supplied. The scientific environment does not require package choices invented by the recipient. Linked installation websites were not in the frozen corpus, so this agreement concerns the documented setup specification rather than independently verified installation.

The default CLI omits the manuscript velocity histogram and signal-loss computation. A source note tells a developer to add quality_stats, but there is no complete ordinary execution sequence for the composed flowchart either. The partial-result anchor is defensible despite the README claim that everything is recomputed.
findings.suggested_correction: Acknowledge the developer instruction to add quality_stats, and explicitly include missing flowchart composition instructions as a reason the all-results instructional anchors are not met.

findings.explanation: The host rerun record declares benchmark, gaze, label and image inputs, allowing acquisition before entering the container. This supports executable assembly. The script get calls are optional no-ops when DataLad is absent, as in the container recipe; they should not be presented as the essential container acquisition mechanism.

Executable targets cover the core analysis and PDF rendering, but the flowchart function is explicitly a non-executed fragment and does not save its plots. Highest coverage is therefore unsupported even though quality_stats itself contains executable code.

The assigned score may remain partial, but its stated reason misapplies the highest anchor, which covers every scoped computation represented in provenance. Histogram/manual-figure computations missing from provenance do not by themselves reduce A-06; they are gaps under T-04/A-03/A-05. The recorded label computation, in contrast, is represented in provenance and requires manual reconstruction of an unrecorded Python environment.
findings.suggested_correction: Retain 2 only with an explicit recorded-computation inventory and the unresolved label-execution environment as the reason. Do not use absence of a provenance record alone as the replay-capability penalty.

findings.explanation: Data modules, reusable implementation, paper analysis, environment and manuscript/figure sources have identifiable responsibilities and separable paths. Manual figure editing does not erase those module boundaries.

Consumers import implementation test utilities and depend on the benchmark repository internal directory layout. Independently selectable gitlinks alone do not establish replaceable interfaces. The limited-interface rating is supported.

Implementation and input modules have attributable terms, whereas labels lack an explicit module declaration in the inspected tree. The partial module-license score follows without presuming that the paper root license applies to a separate repository.

License declarations establish identifiable terms but no inspected composition document addresses how they are combined. Anchor 1 specifically permits this distinction; the review does not infer legal incompatibility.

The raw-data declaration explicitly disclaims registration/authentication, and the required code/data/image routes are presented as ordinary recipient retrieval. No mixed restricted-access boundary is identified within the stated runtime scope. This remains documentary support, not a payload-access test.

Root and nested module declarations identify selections, while concrete analysis paths and the container/Make connection identify how they are composed. Combining these specifications is legitimate under the anchor; a separate dependency-graph format is unnecessary.

The README states tool versions, platforms and approximate downloads. The supplied adapter explicitly notes its assumption that Docker is available on PATH and manageable by a non-root user. That supports the residual host-prerequisite concern, though linked external installation guidance was not available for inspection.

Inspected runtime file accesses are dataset-relative and the adapter chooses its mount from the current directory. Python selection is isolated in configuration. The unreachable lab acquisition path is not consumed by this runtime and is not evidence of an embedded host path here.

The imports and rendering commands examined correspond to declared Python/system packages. DataLad is optional inside the script and supplied at the orchestration layer, so its absence from the image recipe is not an omitted mandatory container dependency. Exact pins are appropriately handled separately.

The present reproduction environment definitions are versioned in the root and pinned implementation module. The missing historical label-environment record is a T-05 gap under this explicitly chosen input/reproduction boundary, not an untracked existing root environment file. Binary normalization and denominator treatment are correct.

The machine-readable image/recipe/configuration path is consumable by the supplied adapter on a compatible Docker host. This supports specification capability; it does not establish successful cross-platform execution or reconstructible frozen package resolution.

The root procedure invokes docker run on a selected image, creating a new mutable container per invocation. This is stronger than merely recommending a virtual environment. The finding should continue to be read as applying to the present root reproduction procedure, not every historical upstream label run.

The adapter mounts the working dataset into the container and uses --rm; the run record is committed outside that mutable container and outputs are directed into the mounted dataset. Thus disposal does not inherently discard the required persisted products or run record.

A fresh clone and declared inputs specify an initial state, while cleanup is incomplete as an automatic isolation mechanism. SVGs remain and the writable dataset is mounted wholesale. In addition, failed runs can leave dockertmp because removal follows &&; mkdir does not itself ensure a fresh HOME. The partial rating appropriately avoids claiming automatic clean-workspace enforcement.

The evidence establishes exact identities and advertised retrieval routes, including image URLs, but the rationale upgrades these to every intended version being obtainable. No payload was obtained in this cohort; a historical local image conversion is not a recipient retrieval record. The method distinguishes actual obtainability from recorded identities, so the complete fulfillment claim remains unresolved.
findings.suggested_correction: Keep the positive route evidence and state which historical or supplied records demonstrate usable recipient retrieval for every essential version. If the frozen evidence cannot responsibly distinguish the highest anchor from unavailable versions, use null with an explicit uncertainty explanation; do not assign 2 merely because acquisition was not attempted.

findings.explanation: The stated lack of an independent recovery route rules out anchor 3, but does not by itself rule out anchor 2, which alternatively accepts immutable bundles. The stored, content-addressed image and its fixed manifests are relevant positive evidence that the rationale does not evaluate as a bundle. Conversely, annex identities alone need not prove durable preservation of all data bytes.
findings.suggested_correction: Explain concretely which essential component lacks an immutable bundle, archive or preservation route. If the supplied frozen image/data distribution satisfies the immutable-bundle alternative for all essential components, use 2; otherwise retain 1 with the specific missing preservation mechanism. Treat the boundary between a checksum-addressed store and an immutable bundle as rubric feedback.

findings.explanation: FROM debian:bookworm-slim and unversioned apt installs require moving resolution; selected Python pins do not fix the full build. A retained deployed image cannot supply a missing reproducible build definition. The low nonzero anchor is supported.

CC BY 4.0, MIT, PDDL and GPLv3 are identified by actual license texts. The absent labels declaration is sufficient to defeat complete module coverage; there is no need to infer that every container dependency lacks its own license file.

The root state jointly fixes module commits and image blob identities. The textual remodnav:latest tag inside the manifest does not make the selected image floating because its configuration and layers are fixed. Retrieval uncertainty belongs under D-01 and does not erase the coherent version selection.

The inspected material does not establish a usable producer/source authentication route for the current executable image. A signed historical result tag is relevant indirect provenance evidence, but its identity was not verified and the current OCI conversion postdates it. Zero is supported as not demonstrated, rather than proof that no signature could ever authenticate the older image.

limitations: Independent inspection of the assigned anonymized assessment only, using rubric commit e8d94d00d904058b8f87c8331cbe32e225a9490f and frozen manifest e3c6253bced7d959cd59873c3d49d166bf5793906bcdf65e49e265076d215499. No peer outputs or other instruments were consulted.

No scientific execution, container build, payload acquisition or network call was performed. Missing image/data/SVG payloads are cohort omissions, not observed remote failures. Current recipient retrieval and rendered/scientific equivalence remain unresolved.

External installation pages, signing-key verification and repository web verification status were not available in the frozen source corpus. The supplied adapter is cited by relative frozen locator and content hash because its source URL uses a version tag rather than an immutable commit.
Read-only Git probes used GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1. The signature block was inspected but cryptographic validity and signer identity were not verified.

The native validator passes the assessment against the exact rubric bytes. Independently checked fixed criterion counts, complete 36 responses, allowed binary values and equal dimension weights; no denominator or arithmetic discrepancy was found. Validation does not establish substantive support, and this review supplies no numeric review score.

The persistence distinction between an immutable image bundle and a single content-addressed hosting service requires clearer application of D-02. Agreement on other findings is methodological review, not human approval.
